title: Dataplane RBAC Adapter for Usage Query Routing and Masking
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a lightweight dataplane RBAC adapter that sits between the analytics query gateway and the metric/storage layer. The adapter enforces tenant- and role-based scoping at query time, applies column/row masking for PII-sensitive usage views, and returns a scoped query plan to the query engine. Goal is to centralize enforcement near the dataplane to reduce duplicated filtering logic in each analytics consumer and enable consistent audit/logging and cacheability.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter validates incoming request tokens and resolves entitlements with <1s median lookup for cached tokens
Per-request policy evaluation produces a scoped query plan (row filters + column masks) that the query engine can apply without additional policy checks
Audit logs emitted for every decision: allow/deny/mask with reason and policy id
Integration tests cover tenant-scoped queries, cross-tenant denial, and PII masking scenarios
No change to external analytics API surface; existing routes continue to function when adapter is enabled behind feature flag
implementation_notes: Adapter will be a standalone Go microservice behind the analytics API gateway; lightweight protobuf contract for query plan
Entitlements backend will primarily read from the existing entitlement cache service (ENG-22011); fall back to sync pull from control-plane on cache miss
Policy format: compile existing attribute-based rules to a small DSL that can express row predicates and column mask operations
Use gRPC + TLS between gateway and adapter for low-latency calls; add short-lived connection pool to avoid reconnect overhead
Expose metrics: decision_latency_ms, cache_hit_ratio, masked_columns_count, denied_requests_count
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start with internal 'redwood-internal' org only
Canary: route 5% of console read queries for that org through adapter for 48 hours and validate metrics
Step-up: expand to additional internal orgs, run privacy regression suite, then to a small set of customer orgs (opt-in)
Full rollout gated on <1% error rate overhead and consistent query latency P50 increase <=10ms
Fallback: gateway has transparent bypass to skip adapter if it returns error or times out; monitored by circuit-breaker with automatic fallback
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy compiler and query-plan generation
Integration tests: end-to-end queries against a staging analytics cluster with sample datasets (tenant A/B/C)
Performance tests: measure added tail latency for common query shapes with KV cache warm vs cold
Security tests: validate masking cannot be bypassed and that audit logs include required fields
Chaos test: simulate adapter timeouts and ensure gateway fallback preserves availability
performance_considerations: Prefer returning a compact query-plan (predicates + mask directives) rather than rewriting SQL to minimize planner churn
Batch entitlement lookups for multi-entity queries to reduce round-trips
Use LRU with TTL tuned to usage patterns; initial TTL 60s and observe eviction rate
Measure memory footprint: target adapter p95 memory < 250MB for a single replica under 1000 qps
Instrument to detect policy-compile hotspots; precompile common policies at startup
risks: Increased query latency if adapter becomes hot path; mitigated by cache/batching and circuit-breaker
Policy mismatch risk between control plane and adapter compiler; mitigate with daily reconciliation job and CI policy compatibility checks
Potential for over-masking (loss of analytic fidelity); include label-driven opt-outs and QA playbook
Operational complexity: adds another service to deploy and monitor; reduce blast radius by starting internal-only and strict SLOs
